components.note: 女 (woman) — marks women, as in 妈, 姐, 好; 姓 first meant the clan traced through mothers.
生 (shēng) hints at the sound: 姓 xìng is close to 性 xìng and 星 xīng, which share it.

example.hanzi: 你姓什么?
example.pinyin: Nǐ xìng shénme?
example.english: What is your surname?
example.fact: 姓 is both a noun (surname) and a verb ('to be surnamed'): 我姓李. The polite way to ask is 您贵姓? Chinese surnames come first and given names second. 老百姓 literally 'old hundred surnames' means ordinary people.

examples.hanzi: 他姓王,叫王小明。
examples.pinyin: Tā xìng Wáng, jiào Wáng Xiǎomíng.
examples.english: His surname is Wang, and he's called Wang Xiaoming.

examples.hanzi: 请问,您贵姓?
examples.pinyin: Qǐngwèn, nín guì xìng?
examples.english: Excuse me, what is your surname?

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做: 作 is something a person does or makes.
乍 (zuò) gives the exact sound; 乍 also in 昨 zuó, 炸 zhà and 怎 zěn.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 室 room, 安 safe, 字 character; 家 is home.
豕 (pig) — a pig under a roof: pigs were kept in the home, hence home and family.

example.hanzi: 她是一位很有名的作家。
example.pinyin: Tā shì yí wèi hěn yǒumíng de zuòjiā.
example.english: She is a very famous author.
example.fact: 家 (literally "home, family") has broadened into a suffix marking expertise or profession — 作家 ("writer"), 画家 ("painter"), 科学家 ("scientist") — functioning much like English "-er" or "-ist" tacked onto a field of activity.

examples.hanzi: 这位作家写过很多儿童故事。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi zuòjiā xiěguo hěn duō értóng gùshi.
examples.english: This author has written many children's stories.

examples.hanzi: 我最喜欢的作家来我们学校做讲座了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuì xǐhuan de zuòjiā lái wǒmen xuéxiào zuò jiǎngzuò le.
examples.english: My favorite writer came to give a talk at our school.

components.note: 舌 (tongue) — 舌 is the tongue, as in 话, 活; 辞 is words and speech, and the same sound as 词 cí.
耳 (ear) — hearing and listening: 听, 闻, 聋; 职 is the duty one hears and remembers.
只 (zhī) is a near sound match for zhí; also in 织 zhī and 识 shí.

example.hanzi: 他因为压力太大决定辞职。
example.pinyin: Tā yīnwèi yālì tài dà juédìng cízhí.
example.english: He decided to resign because the pressure was too great.
example.fact: 辞职 is a verb-object compound — 辞 ("to resign from") plus its own built-in object 职 ("post") — so it's already grammatically "full" and can't take a further direct object; naming a specific job requires inserting another verb, as in 辞去这个职位 ("resign from this position"), rather than tacking the job directly onto 辞职.

examples.hanzi: 他上个月辞职了，现在在找新工作。
examples.pinyin: Tā shàng ge yuè cízhí le, xiànzài zài zhǎo xīn gōngzuò.
examples.english: He resigned last month and is now looking for a new job.

examples.hanzi: 老板不同意她辞职。
examples.pinyin: Lǎobǎn bù tóngyì tā cízhí.
examples.english: The boss doesn't agree to her resigning.

components.note: 衤 (clothing) — 衤 is the clothing radical, as in 衣, 裤, 衬; 被 is a quilt, then the passive marker.
皮 (pí) — loose hint — 被 is bèi; 皮 also sounds out 披 pī and 坡 pō.
口 (mouth) — speaking, as in 说 say, 问 ask; 告 is "to tell". 告 also gives sound to 造 zào and 靠 kào.

example.hanzi: 被告在法庭上保持沉默。
example.pinyin: Bèigào zài fǎtíng shàng bǎochí chénmò.
example.english: The defendant remained silent in court.
example.fact: 被 is Mandarin's passive marker (被 + verb = "to be verbed," as in 被打 "to be hit"), so 被告 literally parses as "the one who is accused" — built the same way as any passive construction — and pairs with its courtroom counterpart 原告 ("the plaintiff," literally "the original accuser").

examples.hanzi: 被告的律师要求重新调查。
examples.pinyin: Bèigào de lǜshī yāoqiú chóngxīn diàochá.
examples.english: The defendant's lawyer asked for a new investigation.

examples.hanzi: 法官问被告有没有什么要说的。
examples.pinyin: Fǎguān wèn bèigào yǒu méiyǒu shénme yào shuō de.
examples.english: The judge asked the defendant whether he had anything to say.

components.note: 钅 (metal) — 钅 is the simplified 金 (metal), as in 铁, 银, 钟; early money was metal coins.
戋 (jiān) — near sound — 钱 is qián; 戋 also sounds out 浅 qiǎn and 线 xiàn, and means small or thin.
勹 (wrap) — a person curled around something; in 包 it wraps around a baby 巳, the original picture. 包 sounds out 抱 bào, 跑 pǎo, 泡 pào, 饱 bǎo.

example.hanzi: 我的钱包不见了!
example.pinyin: Wǒ de qiánbāo bú jiàn le!
example.english: My wallet is missing!
example.fact: 钱包 is about as transparent as compounds get: 钱 ("money," built on the metal radical 钅 since early coins were cast in bronze) plus 包 ("bag," a pictograph of something wrapped up) combine literally into "money bag" — the everyday word for wallet or purse.

examples.hanzi: 他把钱包放在了桌子上。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ qiánbāo fàng zài le zhuōzi shang.
examples.english: He left his wallet on the table.

examples.hanzi: 这个钱包是我妈妈送给我的生日礼物。
examples.pinyin: Zhège qiánbāo shì wǒ māma sòng gěi wǒ de shēngrì lǐwù.
examples.english: This wallet was a birthday present from my mom.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter: 家, 安, 室; a guest is a person under your roof.
各 (gè) is a loose sound clue; same part in 路 lù, 洛 luò, 落 luò.

example.hanzi: 今天晚上有客人来。
example.pinyin: Jīntiān wǎnshang yǒu kèrén lái.
example.english: We have guests coming tonight.
example.fact: 客 is central to Chinese hospitality: 客人 (guest), 客气 (polite), and 不客气 ('you're welcome'). 客厅 is the living room, literally the 'guest hall'. 做客 means to be a guest at someone's home.

examples.hanzi: 欢迎来我家做客。
examples.pinyin: Huānyíng lái wǒ jiā zuòkè.
examples.english: Welcome to my home as a guest.

examples.hanzi: 今天我请客,大家随便点。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān wǒ qǐngkè, dàjiā suíbiàn diǎn.
examples.english: It's my treat today, order whatever you like.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 讠 is the simplified 言 (speech), as in 说, 话, 请; 诚 is honest speech.
成 (chéng) — same sound — 诚 is chéng, like 成; 成 also sounds out 城 chéng.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 字, 室: a house stocked with goods, so solid and real.

example.hanzi: 做人要诚实,不能说谎。
example.pinyin: Zuò rén yào chéngshí, bù néng shuōhuǎng.
example.english: One should be honest and not tell lies.
example.fact: 诚实 describes honesty as a straightforward moral virtue — telling the truth, not lying — while its near-synonym 老实 overlaps in meaning but leans toward "well-behaved, guileless, simple," sometimes carrying a faint hint of naivety that 诚实 doesn't have.

examples.hanzi: 他是一个诚实的孩子，从来不说谎。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì yí ge chéngshí de háizi, cónglái bù shuō huǎng.
examples.english: He is an honest child who never lies.

examples.hanzi: 请你诚实地回答我的问题。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng nǐ chéngshí de huídá wǒ de wèntí.
examples.english: Please answer my question honestly.

components.note: 贝 (shell, money) — 贝 is money and value, as in 财, 买, 贵; 贱 is cheap and low in value.
戋 (jiān) — near sound — 贱 is jiàn; 戋 also hints small, as in 钱 and 浅.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 电视剧里,女主角气得骂对方是贱人。
example.pinyin: Diànshìjù lǐ, nǚzhǔjué qì de mà duìfāng shì jiànrén.
example.english: In the TV drama, the female lead got so angry she called the other woman a "jiànrén."
example.fact: 贱人 is a strongly vulgar, gendered insult, roughly equivalent to "bitch" or "slut" — 贱 ("cheap, lowly, contemptible") plus 人 ("person") combine into a term that gained extra circulation in China through internet slang and viral video clips in the 2010s, and it should be recognized as a genuine insult rather than ordinary vocabulary.

examples.hanzi: 他骂她是贱人，这样说话很不礼貌。
examples.pinyin: Tā mà tā shì jiànrén, zhèyàng shuō huà hěn bù lǐmào.
examples.english: He called her a nasty name, which is very rude.

examples.hanzi: 不要用“贱人”这样难听的话骂别人。
examples.pinyin: Bú yào yòng "jiànrén" zhèyàng nántīng de huà mà biéren.
examples.english: Don't curse at others with ugly words like "jiànrén."

components.note: 合 (join) — a lid fitting over an opening 口: things that fit together. 合 also appears in 答 dá, 给 gěi and 拾 shí.
氵 (water) — water, as in 河, 海, 清: in the old form 灋, water stood for fairness, so law and method.

example.hanzi: 这种做法在很多国家都是合法的。
example.pinyin: Zhèzhǒng zuòfǎ zài hěn duō guójiā dōu shì héfǎ de.
example.english: This practice is legal in many countries.
example.fact: 合法 (literally "conforming to law" — 合 "to match, fit" plus 法 "law") pairs with its direct opposite 非法 ("illegal"), formed with the negating prefix 非-, the same prefix behind other formal antonyms like 非正式 ("informal") and 非官方 ("unofficial").

examples.hanzi: 在这里停车是合法的吗？
examples.pinyin: Zài zhèlǐ tíng chē shì héfǎ de ma?
examples.english: Is it legal to park here?

examples.hanzi: 他们是合法夫妻，有结婚证。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen shì héfǎ fūqī, yǒu jiéhūn zhèng.
examples.english: They are a lawfully married couple and have a marriage certificate.

components.note: 米 (rice, grain) — 米 is rice and grain, as in 粥, 糖, 精; 粉 is flour ground from grain, then powder.
分 (fēn) — same sound, different tone — 粉 is fěn; 分 also sounds out 份 fèn.
纟 (silk, thread) — 纟 is the simplified 糸 (silk); 丝 is the simplified form of 絲, two skeins of silk side by side.

example.hanzi: 他是那个歌手的忠实粉丝。
example.pinyin: Tā shì nàge gēshǒu de zhōngshí fěnsī.
example.english: He is that singer's devoted fan.
example.fact: 粉丝 first meant only mung-bean noodles; its now-dominant sense of "fan, enthusiast" arose only in the 2000s as a phonetic pun on the English word "fans," which happens to sound almost identical — the food meaning came first, and the fandom meaning was borrowed wholesale from English sound alone.

examples.hanzi: 我今晚吃粉丝汤。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jīnwǎn chī fěnsī tāng.
examples.english: I'm having glass noodle soup tonight.

examples.hanzi: 她的微博有一百万粉丝。
examples.pinyin: Tā de wēibó yǒu yì bǎi wàn fěnsī.
examples.english: She has a million followers on Weibo.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — words, as in 说, 请, 诉: you thank someone with words.
射 (shè) is a loose sound clue for xiè; in 谢谢 the tone drops to neutral on the second.
大 (big person) — a person with a line above the head, marking the sky above; tiān = heaven, sky, day.
讠 (speech) — words, as in 说, 请, 诉: you thank someone with words.
射 (shè) is a loose sound clue for xiè; in 谢谢 the tone drops to neutral on the second.
土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 场 field, 城 city, 坐 sit.
也 (yě) is a loose sound clue for dì; 也 also sounds out 他 tā and 池 chí.

example.hanzi: 谢天谢地,飞机没有延误。
example.pinyin: Xiètiānxièdì, fēijī méiyǒu yánwù.
example.english: Thank goodness, the flight wasn't delayed.
example.fact: 谢天谢地 literally means "thank heaven, thank earth" — repeating 谢 ("to thank") across both halves of the fixed cosmic pair 天地 ("heaven and earth") — a structure with prayer-like origins that today functions as a purely secular exclamation of relief, much like English "thank goodness."

examples.hanzi: 谢天谢地，你没事！
examples.pinyin: Xiètiān-xièdì, nǐ méi shì!
examples.english: Thank goodness, you're okay!

examples.hanzi: 谢天谢地，雨终于停了。
examples.pinyin: Xiètiān-xièdì, yǔ zhōngyú tíng le.
examples.english: Thank goodness, the rain has finally stopped.

meanings: (reduplicated, in an urgent plea) please help!

components.note: 攵 (tap, hand with stick) — actions taken on something: 教, 放, 改; 救 is to take action to rescue.
求 (qiú) is a near sound match for jiù; 求 also means ask for help.
攵 (tap, hand with stick) — actions taken on something: 教, 放, 改; 救 is to take action to rescue.
求 (qiú) is a near sound match for jiù; 求 also means ask for help.

example.hanzi: 妈妈,救救我!
example.pinyin: Māma, jiùjiu wǒ!
example.english: Mom, save me!
example.fact: 救救 doubles the single verb 救 ("to save, to rescue") using Mandarin's common VV reduplication pattern — the same pattern that softens a casual request in 看看 ("take a quick look") — but attached to an urgent verb like 救, it instead reads as a plaintive, pleading cry, as in the common exclamation 救救我!("please save me!").

examples.hanzi: 快来救救这只受伤的小鸟！
examples.pinyin: Kuài lái jiùjiu zhè zhī shòushāng de xiǎo niǎo!
examples.english: Come quickly and save this injured little bird!

examples.hanzi: 求求你，救救我的孩子！
examples.pinyin: Qiúqiu nǐ, jiùjiu wǒ de háizi!
examples.english: Please, save my child!

components.note: 纟 (thread, simplified 糸) — silk and cord: 红, 线, 给; 级 first meant the order of threads, then rank.
及 (jí) sounds exactly like 级; also 极 jí, 吸 xī.

example.hanzi: 你在几年级?
example.pinyin: Nǐ zài jǐ niánjí?
example.english: What grade are you in?
example.fact: 级 names levels and ranks: 年级 (school year), 高级 (advanced), 初级 (beginner), 升级 (to upgrade). It is also the measure word for steps and levels, as in language exams and rankings like HSK.

examples.hanzi: 他是我们公司的高级工程师。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì wǒmen gōngsī de gāojí gōngchéngshī.
examples.english: He is a senior engineer at our company.

examples.hanzi: 我的汉语只有初级水平。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de Hànyǔ zhǐ yǒu chūjí shuǐpíng.
examples.english: My Chinese is only at a beginner level.

meanings: to search (a place, a database, online etc)

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand radical for actions done by hand, as in 找 look for, 拿 take, 抓 grab; 搜 is to search by hand.
叟 (sǒu) — same sound family — 搜 is sōu; 叟 also sounds out 艘 sōu.
糸 (thread, traditional of 纟) — silk and cord: 紧 tight, 系 tie; 索 is a twisted rope, seen in 线索 clue.

example.hanzi: 你可以在网上搜索这个问题的答案。
example.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ zài wǎngshàng sōusuǒ zhège wèntí de dá'àn.
example.english: You can search online for the answer to this question.
example.fact: 搜索 is the more formal, technical register of "to search" — the word printed on search-engine buttons and used for database queries or police searches — while everyday casual speech more often reaches for the plainer 查 or 找 to mean the same basic idea of looking something up.

examples.hanzi: 我在网上搜索了很多资料。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài wǎng shang sōusuǒ le hěn duō zīliào.
examples.english: I searched for a lot of information online.

examples.hanzi: 警察正在搜索那座山。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá zhèngzài sōusuǒ nà zuò shān.
examples.english: The police are searching that mountain.

components.note: 女 (woman) — women and family, as in 妈, 她, 姐.
子 (child) — a woman with her child: the picture of something good.
勹 (wrap) — the visible part, a bent shape. Memory aid: a stooped figure under weight, wearing down over time — a long time, as in 好久.
灸 (jiǔ, moxibustion) — 久 is its sound part, same sound jiǔ. Another is 玖 jiǔ. The old picture of 久 is disputed.

example.hanzi: 好久不见,你最近怎样?
example.pinyin: Hǎojiǔ bú jiàn, nǐ zuìjìn zěnyàng?
example.english: Long time no see, how have you been lately?
example.fact: 好久不见 ("long time no see") is one of Mandarin's standard reunion greetings — and the near word-for-word English phrase "long time no see" is widely believed to be a calque borrowed directly from this Chinese expression by Chinese immigrant communities, rather than a coincidence.

examples.hanzi: 我们好久没有一起吃饭了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen hǎojiǔ méiyǒu yìqǐ chī fàn le.
examples.english: We haven't had a meal together in a long time.

examples.hanzi: 你等了好久吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ děng le hǎojiǔ ma?
examples.english: Have you been waiting for a long time?

components.note: 工 (work) — a carpenter's tool shape: work, craftsman. 工 is a sound series: 红 hóng, 江 jiāng, 功 gōng, 空 kōng.
厂 (cliff, shelter) — 厂 is a cliff or overhang and the root of 厅, 原, 厚; the modern meaning "factory" is separate, as in 工厂.

example.hanzi: 这家工厂生产各种电子产品。
example.pinyin: Zhèjiā gōngchǎng shēngchǎn gèzhǒng diànzǐ chǎnpǐn.
example.english: This factory produces all kinds of electronic products.
example.fact: 厂 by itself is a simplified pictograph of a bare lean-to shelter — strokes suggesting a roof over an open space — so 工厂 literally reads as "a building for work," with 厂 also showing up as a component in other structure-related simplified characters like 广.

examples.hanzi: 这家工厂有两千多名工人。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngchǎng yǒu liǎng qiān duō míng gōngrén.
examples.english: This factory has more than two thousand workers.

examples.hanzi: 爸爸在一家汽车工厂上班。
examples.pinyin: Bàba zài yì jiā qìchē gōngchǎng shàngbān.
examples.english: My dad works at a car factory.

components.note: 留 (liú) is a sound clue for 溜 liū, 榴 liú and 瘤 liú; as a word it means to stay or keep.
纟 (thread, simplified 糸) — silk and cord: 红, 线, 组; 给 is to supply thread, then to give.
合 (hé) is only a loose sound clue; same part in 答 dá, 拾 shí, 恰 qià.

example.hanzi: 妈妈把最后一块蛋糕留给了我。
example.pinyin: Māma bǎ zuìhòu yí kuài dàngāo liúgěi le wǒ.
example.english: Mom saved the last piece of cake for me.
example.fact: 留给 attaches the complement 给 ("to, for") onto the verb 留 ("to keep, leave behind") specifically to name a recipient — commonly slotted into the 把...留给... construction ("set X aside for Y"), a verb-complement pattern that makes clear who the leftover or saved item is meant for.

examples.hanzi: 这些书我想留给我的孙子。
examples.pinyin: Zhèxiē shū wǒ xiǎng liúgěi wǒ de sūnzi.
examples.english: I want to leave these books to my grandson.

examples.hanzi: 老师把靠窗的座位留给了新同学。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī bǎ kào chuāng de zuòwèi liúgěi le xīn tóngxué.
examples.english: The teacher saved the seat by the window for the new classmate.

components.note: 走 (walk, run) — a person with swinging arms above a foot 止. As a radical it marks movement: 起, 越, 超, 趣.
辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过, 进, 送; 运 is to move, then to be moved by luck.
云 (yún) is a near sound match for yùn.

example.hanzi: 今天真走运,我捡到了一百块钱。
example.pinyin: Jīntiān zhēn zǒuyùn, wǒ jiǎndào le yìbǎi kuài qián.
example.english: I got really lucky today — I found a hundred yuan.
example.fact: 运 carries both "to move, transport" and "fortune, destiny" as core senses (as in 运气, "luck"), so 走运 pictures good fortune as something that walks toward you — paired with the opposite construction 倒霉 ("to have bad luck"), where 倒 means "to fall, overturn," picturing misfortune instead as something toppling over.

examples.hanzi: 今天真走运，刚到车站就来了一辆车。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān zhēn zǒuyùn, gāng dào chēzhàn jiù lái le yí liàng chē.
examples.english: I'm really in luck today; a bus came just as I got to the stop.

examples.hanzi: 你真走运，最后一张票被你买到了。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zhēn zǒuyùn, zuìhòu yì zhāng piào bèi nǐ mǎi dào le.
examples.english: You're lucky; you got the very last ticket.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — breath and speech: 呼, 吃, 喝; 吸 is to breathe in.
及 (jí) is a loose sound hint for xī; same part in 级 jí and 极 jí.
龶 (plant-like top) — dictionary reads the top as 'a poisonous plant'. Memory aid: a plant growing on top of a mother (母) is something you must not eat.
母 (mǔ, mother) — the bottom part and radical. Sound clue is lost today (毒 is dú); use it as a visual memory aid, as in 母亲.

example.hanzi: 吸毒对身体的伤害非常大。
example.pinyin: Xīdú duì shēntǐ de shānghài fēicháng dà.
example.english: Drug use causes very serious harm to the body.
example.fact: 吸毒 literally means "to inhale poison" — 吸 ("to breathe in") plus 毒 ("poison, toxin") — a compound rooted in inhaling or smoking a substance, even though the word is now used broadly for illegal drug use regardless of whether it's actually inhaled, injected, or swallowed.

examples.hanzi: 吸毒会毁掉一个人的一生。
examples.pinyin: Xīdú huì huǐdiào yí ge rén de yìshēng.
examples.english: Taking drugs can ruin a person's whole life.

examples.hanzi: 他因为吸毒被送进了戒毒所。
examples.pinyin: Tā yīnwèi xīdú bèi sòng jìn le jièdúsuǒ.
examples.english: He was sent to a rehab center for taking drugs.

components.note: 犭 (dog, beast) — animals: 狗, 猫, 狼; 独 first meant a solitary animal, then alone.
The old sound part 蜀 (shǔ) is also in 属 shǔ, 烛 zhú and 触 chù; simplified 独 shows 虫 instead.
立 (stand) — a person standing on the ground line. As a radical it appears in 站 stand, 位 seat, 竟; also in 建立 establish.

example.hanzi: 这个国家最终获得了独立。
example.pinyin: Zhège guójiā zuìzhōng huòdé le dúlì.
example.english: This country finally gained independence.
example.fact: 独立 literally means "to stand alone" — 独 ("single, solitary") plus 立 (a pictograph of a person standing upright on the ground) — and covers the same ground in Chinese that English splits between a nation's political independence and a person's personal self-reliance, both expressed with this one compound.

examples.hanzi: 我想过一种独立的生活。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng guò yì zhǒng dúlì de shēnghuó.
examples.english: I want to live an independent life.

examples.hanzi: 这个孩子已经可以独立完成作业了。
examples.pinyin: Zhège háizi yǐjīng kěyǐ dúlì wánchéng zuòyè le.
examples.english: This child can already finish homework independently.

components.note: 至 (arrive) — 到 is to arrive.
刂 is the knife form 刀 (dāo), a close sound clue for dào; 到 itself sounds out 倒 dǎo/dào.
来 (come) — it began as a picture of a wheat plant; the sound was borrowed for "come". 麦 (wheat) still shows it, with a root 夂 added.

example.hanzi: 大家都在期待春天的到来。
example.pinyin: Dàjiā dōu zài qídài chūntiān de dàolái.
example.english: Everyone is looking forward to the arrival of spring.
example.fact: 到来 often functions almost like a noun, especially in the pattern ...的到来 ("the advent/arrival of...") used for the onset of a season, era, or event — carrying a touch more weight or ceremony than the plainer verb 到 or 来到, which read as a simpler, everyday "to arrive."

examples.hanzi: 新年的到来让大家都很兴奋。
examples.pinyin: Xīnnián de dàolái ràng dàjiā dōu hěn xīngfèn.
examples.english: The arrival of the New Year made everyone excited.

examples.hanzi: 客人到来之前，我们得先打扫房间。
examples.pinyin: Kèrén dàolái zhīqián, wǒmen děi xiān dǎsǎo fángjiān.
examples.english: We have to clean the room before the guests arrive.

components.note: 木 (tree) — wood, as in 树, 桌, 板: 查 first meant a raft of wood. 查 also gives 渣 zhā and 楂 zhā.
木 (tree) — wood, as in 树, 桌, 板: 查 first meant a raft of wood. 查 also gives 渣 zhā and 楂 zhā.

example.hanzi: 这个数据不对,你查查看。
example.pinyin: Zhège shùjù bú duì, nǐ chácha kàn.
example.english: This data is wrong — go check it.
example.fact: 查查 doubles the verb 查 ("to check, look up") the same way 看看 doubles 看 ("to look") — Mandarin's common VV pattern that turns a command into something more casual, "just go take a quick look," rather than a heavier, formal order to investigate; it's often extended to 查查看, tacking on 看 ("and see") for the same casual effect.

examples.hanzi: 你去查查明天的天气吧。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ qù chácha míngtiān de tiānqì ba.
examples.english: Go and check tomorrow's weather.

examples.hanzi: 这个字我不认识，我得查查字典。
examples.pinyin: Zhège zì wǒ bú rènshi, wǒ děi chácha zìdiǎn.
examples.english: I don't know this character, so I need to look it up in the dictionary.

components.note: 冫 (ice) — here the ice form of 氵 (water): 决 first meant to break a dam, so a decisive break.
夬 (guài) is a loose sound clue for jué; 夬 also sounds out 快 kuài and 块 kuài.
贝 (cowrie) — money and value, as in 财, 货, 买: competing for prizes was once tied to offerings and stakes.

example.hanzi: 我们的球队进入了这次比赛的决赛。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen de qiúduì jìnrù le zhècì bǐsài de juésài.
example.english: Our team advanced to the finals of this competition.
example.fact: 决赛 literally means "the decisive match" — 决 ("to decide, settle") plus 赛 ("competition") — sitting at the top of a family of tournament-stage words built the same way: 初赛 ("preliminary round"), 半决赛 ("semifinal," literally "half-decisive-match"), and 决赛 itself, the final round that settles everything.

examples.hanzi: 决赛将在周日晚上举行。
examples.pinyin: Juésài jiāng zài zhōurì wǎnshang jǔxíng.
examples.english: The final will be held on Sunday evening.

examples.hanzi: 她在游泳决赛中拿了第二名。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài yóuyǒng juésài zhōng ná le dì-èr míng.
examples.english: She won second place in the swimming final.

components.note: 手 (hand) — a picture of a hand with fingers spread. As a left-hand radical it becomes 扌 in 打 hit, 拿 take, 推 push.
殳 (strike) — 殳 is a hand with a tool striking, as in 毁, 殴; 段 is a piece cut off a larger whole, and sounds out 锻 duàn.

example.hanzi: 他用了各种手段来达到自己的目的。
example.pinyin: Tā yòng le gèzhǒng shǒuduàn lái dádào zìjǐ de mùdì.
example.english: He used every kind of means to achieve his own goal.
example.fact: 手段 sits on a sliding scale from neutral "method" to outright "scheming" depending on context — 谈判手段 ("negotiating tactics") is fine, but 使手段 ("to pull tricks") is openly critical — a shade of cunning its more purely neutral near-synonym 方法 ("method, approach") doesn't carry.

examples.hanzi: 我们需要想一个更好的手段来解决问题。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xūyào xiǎng yí ge gèng hǎo de shǒuduàn lái jiějué wèntí.
examples.english: We need to think of a better way to solve the problem.

examples.hanzi: 你不能用这种手段骗人。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bù néng yòng zhè zhǒng shǒuduàn piàn rén.
examples.english: You can't use this kind of trick to cheat people.

components.note: 食 (food, eat) — a lid over a bowl of food. As a left-hand radical it becomes 饣: 饭 meal, 饿 hungry, 饱 full, 饺 dumpling.

example.hanzi: 这里的食物很好吃。
example.pinyin: Zhèlǐ de shíwù hěn hǎochī.
example.english: The food here is very delicious.
example.fact: In everyday speech 'to eat' is 吃, while 食 is the formal and bound form: 食物 (food), 食堂 (canteen), 素食 (vegetarian food). The saying 民以食为天 means food is heaven to the people.

examples.hanzi: 中国的饮食文化很丰富。
examples.pinyin: Zhōngguó de yǐnshí wénhuà hěn fēngfù.
examples.english: Chinese food culture is very rich.

examples.hanzi: 晚上少吃零食对身体好。
examples.pinyin: Wǎnshang shǎo chī língshí duì shēntǐ hǎo.
examples.english: Eating fewer snacks at night is good for your health.

components.note: 扌 (hand, 提手旁) — marks hand actions, as in 打 hit, 推 push, 拉 pull; 扣 is buttoning or pulling tight.
口 (kǒu) — close sound: 扣 kòu. 口 here is both mouth and the sound clue.

example.hanzi: 请把扣子扣好。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ kòuzi kòu hǎo.
example.english: Please button up properly.
example.fact: 扣 is the verb 'to fasten', and 扣子 is the button. It also means 'to deduct': 扣钱 (deduct pay), 扣分 (deduct points). In shops, 折扣 is a discount, but 打八折 means 20% off because 八折 is 80% of the price.

examples.hanzi: 外面冷,把外套扣上吧。
examples.pinyin: Wàimiàn lěng, bǎ wàitào kòu shàng ba.
examples.english: It's cold outside, button up your coat.

examples.hanzi: 迟到会被扣工资。
examples.pinyin: Chídào huì bèi kòu gōngzī.
examples.english: Being late will get your pay docked.

components.note: 页 (head) — heads and faces, as in 头, 题, 顶: to turn the head and look.
厄 stands in for 雇 (gù) in the traditional 顧; the clue is only loose today.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter: 家, 安, 室; a guest is a person under your roof.
各 (gè) is a loose sound clue; same part in 路 lù, 洛 luò, 落 luò.

example.hanzi: 这家商店的顾客非常多。
example.pinyin: Zhèjiā shāngdiàn de gùkè fēicháng duō.
example.english: This store has a huge number of customers.
example.fact: 客 (literally "guest," someone welcomed under a roof) turns up as a suffix across a whole family of words for visitors and users — 顾客 ("customer," someone "looked after" as a guest), 游客 ("tourist"), 房客 ("tenant, lodger") — framing each relationship through the lens of hospitality rather than transaction.

examples.hanzi: 顾客可以随时退货。
examples.pinyin: Gùkè kěyǐ suíshí tuìhuò.
examples.english: Customers can return goods at any time.

examples.hanzi: 服务员对每位顾客都很热情。
examples.pinyin: Fúwùyuán duì měi wèi gùkè dōu hěn rèqíng.
examples.english: The waiter is friendly to every customer.

components.note: 农 (farming) — simplified from 農, which showed a tool 辰 working a field 田; 农 is farming, as in 农民.
土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 地, 城, 坐: a field or open space.
昜 (yáng) is the traditional sound part, a loose clue for chǎng; the same part is in 汤 tāng, 扬 yáng and 肠 cháng.

example.hanzi: 爷爷在乡下有一个小农场。
example.pinyin: Yéye zài xiāngxià yǒu yí gè xiǎo nóngchǎng.
example.english: Grandpa has a small farm out in the countryside.
example.fact: 场 (literally "an open plot of ground") is a productive suffix for naming venues built on open space — 农场 ("farm"), 操场 ("sports field"), 停车场 ("parking lot") — all reusing the same character for a flat, open-air area, just filled with a different purpose each time.

examples.hanzi: 这个农场养了很多牛和羊。
examples.pinyin: Zhège nóngchǎng yǎng le hěn duō niú hé yáng.
examples.english: This farm raises many cows and sheep.

examples.hanzi: 周末我们带孩子去农场摘草莓。
examples.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒmen dài háizi qù nóngchǎng zhāi cǎoméi.
examples.english: On the weekend we take the kids to the farm to pick strawberries.

components.note: 网 (net) — a picture of a hanging net with crossing cords; as a radical it appears as 罒 in 罚, 置, 罗.
纟 (silk, thread) — 纟 is the simplified 糸 (thread), as in 红, 给; 络 is a net of threads, as in 网络.
各 (gè) — near sound — 络 is luò; 各 also sounds out 洛 luò and 路 lù.

example.hanzi: 现在几乎每个人都离不开网络。
example.pinyin: Xiànzài jīhū měi gè rén dōu lí bu kāi wǎngluò.
example.english: Nowadays almost everyone can't do without the Internet.
example.fact: 网 is a pictograph of a woven net, and 络 (built on the thread radical 纟) names an interconnected web of threads or veins — together 网络 already meant "a connected mesh" well before computers existed, which is why the word slotted so naturally onto "network" and "the Internet" once the technology arrived.

examples.hanzi: 我家的网络今天特别慢。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiā de wǎngluò jīntiān tèbié màn.
examples.english: The internet at my home is especially slow today.

examples.hanzi: 网络上的消息不一定都是真的。
examples.pinyin: Wǎngluò shang de xiāoxi bù yídìng dōu shì zhēn de.
examples.english: Not everything you read online is true.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — a picture of an open mouth; as a radical it appears in characters of speech, eating and sounds — 吃, 喝, 叫, 吗.
衣 (clothing, cloth) — clothes and cloth: 装, 被, 衬; 袋 is a bag made of cloth.
代 (dài) sounds exactly like 袋; also in 贷 dài.

example.hanzi: 他把钥匙放进了裤子口袋里。
example.pinyin: Tā bǎ yàoshi fàngjìn le kùzi kǒudài lǐ.
example.english: He put the keys into his pants pocket.
example.fact: 口 ("mouth, opening") plus 袋 ("bag," built on the clothing radical 衣) literally describes a pocket or sack by its most functional feature — the opening you reach into — the same logic behind other 口-compounds like 瓶口 ("the mouth of a bottle") and 门口 ("doorway, entrance").

examples.hanzi: 我的口袋里只有几块钱。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de kǒudài lǐ zhǐyǒu jǐ kuài qián.
examples.english: I only have a few yuan in my pocket.

examples.hanzi: 外套的口袋太小，放不下手机。
examples.pinyin: Wàitào de kǒudài tài xiǎo, fàng bú xià shǒujī.
examples.english: The jacket pocket is too small to hold a phone.

components.note: 方 (square, direction) — early picture is disputed (a plough-like tool or lashed boats). Sound clue in 房 fáng, 防 fáng, 访 fǎng, 放 fàng.
亠 (lid) — the top. Memory aid: a lid over a bent shape — a square-cornered 'side' or place, as in 地方, 方法.
亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do. 便 is a person adjusting things 更 to make them convenient (traditional explanation).

example.hanzi: 手机让我们的生活变得更加方便。
example.pinyin: Shǒujī ràng wǒmen de shēnghuó biàn de gèngjiā fāngbiàn.
example.english: Smartphones have made our lives more convenient.
example.fact: Beyond meaning "convenient," 方便 doubles as Mandarin's most common polite euphemism for using the restroom — 我想去方便一下 ("I'd like to go and, ah, take care of things") sidesteps blunter terms, the same instinct behind English stand-ins like "powder my nose."

examples.hanzi: 你什么时候方便？我们见个面吧。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ shénme shíhou fāngbiàn? Wǒmen jiàn ge miàn ba.
examples.english: When is convenient for you? Let's meet up.

examples.hanzi: 这里买东西很方便，楼下就有超市。
examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ mǎi dōngxi hěn fāngbiàn, lóu xià jiù yǒu chāoshì.
examples.english: Shopping is convenient here; there's a supermarket downstairs.

components.note: 日 (sun) — day and time, as in 晴 clear, 早 early, 明 bright; time was read from the sun.
寸 (cùn) stands in for 寺 sì in the traditional 時; sound clue is loose. 寺 also gives 诗 shī and 持 chí.
木 (tree) — wood, as in 树, 林, 桌; the older meaning was a wooden mechanism.
几 (jī) gives the exact sound; also in 饥 jī and 肌 jī.

example.hanzi: 现在正是投资的好时机。
example.pinyin: Xiànzài zhèng shì tóuzī de hǎo shíjī.
example.english: Right now is a great opportunity for investment.
example.fact: 时机 zeroes in specifically on timing — the moment being right for something, as in 抓住时机 ("seize the opportune moment") — while its broader near-synonym 机会 ("opportunity, chance") just names a favorable chance existing at all, without necessarily emphasizing when.

examples.hanzi: 你来得正好，这是个好时机。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ lái de zhènghǎo, zhè shì ge hǎo shíjī.
examples.english: You came at just the right time; this is a good opportunity.

examples.hanzi: 他一直在等待合适的时机。
examples.pinyin: Tā yìzhí zài děngdài héshì de shíjī.
examples.english: He has been waiting for the right moment.

components.note: 毛 (hair) — a picture of a tuft of hair or fur; used in 毛巾 and 毛病 (a flaw).
疒 (illness, 病字旁) — sickness and pain: 疼 ache, 痛 pain, 瘦 thin; here the word for illness itself.
丙 (bǐng) is a near sound match for bìng; also in 柄 bǐng handle.

example.hanzi: 这台电脑最近总出毛病。
example.pinyin: Zhètái diànnǎo zuìjìn zǒng chū máobìng.
example.english: This computer has kept having problems lately.
example.fact: 毛病 stretches informally across three different kinds of trouble that English keeps as separate words — a mechanical glitch (电脑出毛病, "the computer's acting up"), a recurring health ailment (老毛病), and a personal character flaw (坏毛病, "a bad habit") — all covered by this one colloquial term.

examples.hanzi: 这辆车有点毛病，需要修一修。
examples.pinyin: Zhè liàng chē yǒudiǎn máobìng, xūyào xiū yi xiū.
examples.english: There's something wrong with this car; it needs repair.

examples.hanzi: 他有个坏毛病，就是爱迟到。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǒu ge huài máobìng, jiù shì ài chídào.
examples.english: He has a bad habit: he loves being late.

components.note: 子 (child) — children and offspring: 孩 child, 学 study, 孙 grandchild; 存 means to keep or survive.
才 (cái) is only a loose sound hint for cún.

example.hanzi: 我想把钱存在银行里。
example.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng bǎ qián cún zài yínháng lǐ.
example.english: I want to deposit money in the bank.
example.fact: 存 covers keeping, saving and existing: 存钱 (deposit money), 存款 (savings), 保存 (to save a file), 存在 (to exist), 存包 (check a bag). Computer users say 存 for saving a document.

examples.hanzi: 我的手机存了很多照片。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de shǒujī cún le hěn duō zhàopiàn.
examples.english: My phone has lots of photos stored on it.

examples.hanzi: 请把文件存在桌面上。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ wénjiàn cún zài zhuōmiàn shang.
examples.english: Please save the file on the desktop.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — 香 originally combined grain with 甘 (sweet): the smell of cooked grain, in modern writing 日 stands in for 甘.

example.hanzi: 这朵花很香。
example.pinyin: Zhè duǒ huā hěn xiāng.
example.english: This flower smells lovely.
example.fact: 香 means good-smelling and also appetizing: 好香 is said of both flowers and food. It builds 香水 (perfume), 香蕉 (banana) and 香港 (Hong Kong, 'fragrant harbor'). 烧香 (burning incense) is a temple custom.

examples.hanzi: 厨房里有一股香味。
examples.pinyin: Chúfáng li yǒu yì gǔ xiāngwèi.
examples.english: There's a delicious smell in the kitchen.

examples.hanzi: 这个面包闻起来真香!
examples.pinyin: Zhège miànbāo wén qǐlái zhēn xiāng!
examples.english: This bread smells so good!

components.note: 白 (bái) hints at the sound: 百 bǎi is close, and 白 also gives 拍 pāi and 伯 bó.

example.hanzi: 这本书有三百页。
example.pinyin: Zhè běn shū yǒu sānbǎi yè.
example.english: This book has three hundred pages.
example.fact: 百 also means 'all, many': 百货 (department store goods), 百姓 (common people), 百科 (encyclopedic). Percentages use 百分之: 百分之五十 is fifty percent. Note 一百 is yìbǎi with a changed tone for 一.

examples.hanzi: 这条街有一百多家店。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo jiē yǒu yìbǎi duō jiā diàn.
examples.english: This street has over a hundred shops.

examples.hanzi: 这家百货公司在市中心。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā bǎihuò gōngsī zài shìzhōngxīn.
examples.english: This department store is downtown.

components.note: 卩 (kneeling person) — a hand 爪 pressing on a person 卩: to stamp or press a mark, hence seal and print.
广 (building) — 广 is a building radical, as in 店, 床; 度 also sounds out 渡 dù and 镀 dù.

example.hanzi: 印度是世界上人口最多的国家之一。
example.pinyin: Yìndù shì shìjiè shàng rénkǒu zuì duō de guójiā zhīyī.
example.english: India is one of the most populous countries in the world.
example.fact: 印度 comes from a phonetic transliteration that the Tang-dynasty monk Xuanzang recorded in his travelogue 大唐西域记 as a more accurate rendering of the local name than earlier Chinese terms like 身毒 — an older name, 天竺, remained in popular use for centuries afterward regardless, most famously in the novel Journey to the West.

examples.hanzi: 印度的食物以香料闻名。
examples.pinyin: Yìndù de shíwù yǐ xiāngliào wénmíng.
examples.english: Indian food is famous for its spices.

examples.hanzi: 我朋友下个月要去印度工作。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ péngyou xià ge yuè yào qù Yìndù gōngzuò.
examples.english: My friend is going to work in India next month.

components.note: 交 (cross, hand over) — a person with legs crossed: to intersect, then to exchange. Same part in 校 xiào, 较 jiào, 胶 jiāo.
氵 (water) — 氵 is water, as in 河, 海, 汤; 流 is flowing water.
㐬 (liú) — same sound — 流 is liú; 㐬 also sounds out 琉 liú and 硫 liú.

example.hanzi: 两国之间的文化交流越来越多。
example.pinyin: Liǎngguó zhījiān de wénhuà jiāoliú yuè lái yuè duō.
example.english: Cultural exchange between the two countries is increasing.
example.fact: 交 pictures a person standing with legs crossed — an image of intersection and exchange — and 流 means "to flow" (built on the water radical 氵); 交流 combines them into "crossing and flowing," an image of back-and-forth movement equally apt for river currents and for a genuine two-way conversation.

examples.hanzi: 学外语最好多和别人交流。
examples.pinyin: Xué wàiyǔ zuìhǎo duō hé biéren jiāoliú.
examples.english: When learning a foreign language, it's best to communicate with others often.

examples.hanzi: 我们在网上交流学习经验。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zài wǎng shang jiāoliú xuéxí jīngyàn.
examples.english: We exchange study experiences online.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 讠 is the simplified 言 (speech), as in 说, 话; 辩 puts two 辛 (offenders) with words between them, an argument.
扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱: guarding with the hands.
户 (hù, door) gives the exact sound; 户 means door or household.

example.hanzi: 律师在法庭上为被告辩护。
example.pinyin: Lǜshī zài fǎtíng shàng wèi bèigào biànhù.
example.english: The lawyer argued in defense of the defendant in court.
example.fact: 辩护 specifically names defending someone through argument or speech — a lawyer's courtroom defense, or defending a position in a debate — while 保护 ("to protect") covers physical or practical shielding from harm; English's single word "defend" blurs a distinction Chinese keeps clearly separate.

examples.hanzi: 他请了最好的律师为自己辩护。
examples.pinyin: Tā qǐng le zuì hǎo de lǜshī wèi zìjǐ biànhù.
examples.english: He hired the best lawyer to defend him.

examples.hanzi: 你不用为他辩护，他自己知道错了。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ búyòng wèi tā biànhù, tā zìjǐ zhīdào cuò le.
examples.english: You don't need to defend him; he knows he was wrong.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 拿, 抱, 把; 打 is to hit.
丁 (dīng) is a loose sound clue for dǎ; 丁 also sounds out 订 dìng, 顶 dǐng and 钉 dīng.
扌 (hand) — hand radical — 扮 is to dress or act.
分 (fēn) — loose hint — 扮 is bàn; 分 also sounds out 盼 pàn.

example.hanzi: 她精心打扮,准备去参加婚礼。
example.pinyin: Tā jīngxīn dǎban, zhǔnbèi qù cānjiā hūnlǐ.
example.english: She dressed up carefully, getting ready to attend the wedding.
example.fact: 打 in 打扮 functions as one of Mandarin's most productive "light verbs" — the same 打 that appears in 打电话 ("make a phone call") and 打篮球 ("play basketball") — contributing almost no meaning of its own beyond loosely signaling "to do, to perform," which trips up learners who expect 打 to always mean "to hit."

examples.hanzi: 她每天早上都要打扮一个小时。
examples.pinyin: Tā měi tiān zǎoshang dōu yào dǎban yí ge xiǎoshí.
examples.english: She spends an hour getting dressed up every morning.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们把圣诞树打扮得很漂亮。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen bǎ shèngdànshù dǎban de hěn piàoliang.
examples.english: The children decorated the Christmas tree beautifully.

components.note: 日 (sun) — marks sun, daylight and time, as in 明 bright, 晚 evening, 早 early; 晕 is a halo around the sun, then dizzy.
军 (jūn) — loose sound hint (yūn vs jūn); same part in 运 yùn.

example.hanzi: 我头有点晕。
example.pinyin: Wǒ tóu yǒudiǎn yūn.
example.english: I feel a little dizzy.
example.fact: 晕 is 'dizzy' as in 头晕, and 晕倒 means to faint. Motion sickness words, 晕车 (carsick) and 晕船 (seasick), are normally read yùn, the same reading used in 光晕 (halo).

examples.hanzi: 坐船的时候我会晕船。
examples.pinyin: Zuò chuán de shíhou wǒ huì yùnchuán.
examples.english: I get seasick when I'm on a boat.

examples.hanzi: 他看到血就晕倒了。
examples.pinyin: Tā kàndào xuè jiù yūndǎo le.
examples.english: He fainted at the sight of blood.

components.note: 走 (walk, run) — movement, as in 赶 chase, 超 surpass, 越 cross over; 起 is to rise or get up.
己 (jǐ) is a loose sound clue for qǐ; 己 also sounds out 记 jì and 纪 jì.
石 (stone) — stones and minerals: 破, 研, 砖; 码 first meant stone weights, then numbers.
马 (mǎ) sounds exactly like 码; also in 吗, 骂 mà, 妈 mā.

example.hanzi: 这件事起码需要三天才能完成。
example.pinyin: Zhèjiàn shì qǐmǎ xūyào sān tiān cái néng wánchéng.
example.english: This task will take at least three days to finish.
example.fact: 码 broadly means "a numerical marker or code" (号码 "number," 密码 "password"), so 起码 literally suggests "the starting mark" — a baseline value things don't fall below — which lines up neatly with its modern sense as an adverb meaning "at the very least."

examples.hanzi: 你起码应该先打个电话。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ qǐmǎ yīnggāi xiān dǎ ge diànhuà.
examples.english: You should at least have called first.

examples.hanzi: 这双鞋起码要一百块。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shuāng xié qǐmǎ yào yì bǎi kuài.
examples.english: These shoes cost at least a hundred yuan.

components.note: 黄 (huáng) — yellow; as a part it sounds out 簧 huáng and 磺 huáng.

example.hanzi: 秋天树叶都变黄了。
example.pinyin: Qiūtiān shùyè dōu biàn huáng le.
example.english: In autumn the leaves all turn yellow.
example.fact: Yellow was the imperial color of China. 黄河 is the Yellow River, and Chinese people are often called 'descendants of the Yellow Emperor'. 黄 has slang meanings too: 黄色 can mean pornographic, and 黄了 means a plan fell through.

examples.hanzi: 我想买一件黄色的外套。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng mǎi yí jiàn huángsè de wàitào.
examples.english: I want to buy a yellow coat.

examples.hanzi: 看到黄灯就要慢慢停下来。
examples.pinyin: Kàndào huángdēng jiù yào mànmàn tíng xiàlái.
examples.english: When you see a yellow light, slow down and stop.

components.note: 女 (woman) — 女 marks women and feelings in old forms, as in 妒, 嫉; 嫌 is to dislike.
兼 (jiān) — near sound — 嫌 is xián; 兼 also sounds out 谦 qiān and 歉 qiàn.
犭 (beast, form of 犬 dog) — animals: 狗 dog, 猫 cat, 狼 wolf; 犯 is to attack or violate, hence offend.

example.hanzi: 警方正在寻找这起案件的嫌犯。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng zhèngzài xúnzhǎo zhèqǐ ànjiàn de xiánfàn.
example.english: The police are currently searching for the suspect in this case.
example.fact: 嫌犯 is a shortened form of the fuller legal term 嫌疑犯 ("suspected criminal") — 嫌 means "to suspect, to doubt" — so it names someone merely under suspicion, legally and linguistically distinct from 犯人 ("convict"), the word reserved for someone already found guilty.

examples.hanzi: 嫌犯已经被警察抓住了。
examples.pinyin: Xiánfàn yǐjīng bèi jǐngchá zhuā zhù le.
examples.english: The suspect has been caught by the police.

examples.hanzi: 警察把嫌犯带回了警察局。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá bǎ xiánfàn dài huí le jǐngchájú.
examples.english: The police took the suspect back to the station.

components.note: 公 (public) — 八 over 厶: dividing 八 what is private 厶; so "shared, public, fair".
廾 (two hands) — in 開 two hands lift the bar of a gate; 开 is the simplified shape. Compare 关 (close).

example.hanzi: 这个消息还没有公开。
example.pinyin: Zhège xiāoxi hái méiyǒu gōngkāi.
example.english: This piece of news hasn't been made public yet.
example.fact: 公开 does triple grammatical duty — adjective ("public," as in 公开的信息 "public information"), verb ("to make public, to reveal," as in 公开这个消息 "release this news"), and adverb ("openly," as in 公开反对 "openly oppose") — one word covering categories English splits into three separate terms.

examples.hanzi: 这次会议是公开的，谁都可以参加。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì huìyì shì gōngkāi de, shéi dōu kěyǐ cānjiā.
examples.english: This meeting is open to the public, so anyone can attend.

examples.hanzi: 他公开向大家道歉了。
examples.pinyin: Tā gōngkāi xiàng dàjiā dàoqiàn le.
examples.english: He apologized to everyone publicly.

components.note: 彳 (step) — left half of a crossroads: 行 pictures a crossroads, so to go, and (háng) a row or trade.
木 (tree) — 木 is tree, as in 桃, 林, 树; 李 is the plum tree.
子 (zǐ) — near sound — 李 is lǐ; 子 also sounds out 仔 zǐ.

example.hanzi: 上飞机前,请检查一下你的行李。
example.pinyin: Shàng fēijī qián, qǐng jiǎnchá yíxià nǐ de xíngli.
example.english: Before boarding the plane, please check your luggage.
example.fact: 行 ("to travel") carries the obvious half of the meaning, but 李 here is generally understood to be a phonetic loan unrelated to its everyday sense "plum" (or the common surname Li) — some accounts trace 行李 back to an older form 行理, "travel affairs," with 李 gradually substituting for 理 as a sound-alike character.

examples.hanzi: 我的行李太重了，你能帮我吗？
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de xíngli tài zhòng le, nǐ néng bāng wǒ ma?
examples.english: My luggage is too heavy; can you help me?

examples.hanzi: 行李放在后备厢里了。
examples.pinyin: Xíngli fàng zài hòubèixiāng lǐ le.
examples.english: The luggage is in the trunk.

components.note: 王 (jade) — 王 on the left is 玉 (jade), as in 球, 现; 玛瑙 is agate.
马 (mǎ) — same sound — 玛 is mǎ, like 马.
丽 (beautiful) — simplified 麗, which showed a deer 鹿 with antlers, a symbol of grace. Seen in 美丽.

example.hanzi: 玛丽是我在美国认识的一个朋友。
example.pinyin: Mǎlì shì wǒ zài Měiguó rènshi de yí gè péngyou.
example.english: Mary is a friend I met in the United States.
example.fact: 玛丽 is a phonetic transliteration chosen for sound but also for flattering meaning — 玛 ("agate," a gemstone written with the jade radical 王) and 丽 ("beautiful," from an older character depicting a deer's ornate antlers) — a common double duty when rendering foreign women's names into Chinese, picking characters that sound right and read as attractive.

examples.hanzi: 玛丽正在学中文。
examples.pinyin: Mǎlì zhèngzài xué Zhōngwén.
examples.english: Mary is learning Chinese.

examples.hanzi: 你认识玛丽吗？她是我同事。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ rènshi Mǎlì ma? Tā shì wǒ tóngshì.
examples.english: Do you know Mary? She is my coworker.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — 宀 is a roof, as in 家, 室, 安; 宁 is peace and calm at home.
丁 (dīng) — near sound — 宁 is níng; 丁 also sounds out 订 dìng and 厅 tīng.
心 (heart) — wishes and feelings, as in 想, 思, 感: 愿 is what the heart wants.
原 (yuán) is a close sound clue for yuàn; 原 also in 源 yuán.

example.hanzi: 我宁愿走路,也不想挤公交车。
example.pinyin: Wǒ nìngyuàn zǒulù, yě bù xiǎng jǐ gōngjiāochē.
example.english: I'd rather walk than squeeze onto the bus.
example.fact: 宁愿 typically appears in the paired pattern "宁愿…也不/也不要…" to state a preference between two options ("would rather X than Y") — English "would rather...than" compares directly, while Chinese explicitly negates the rejected option instead.

examples.hanzi: 我宁愿多花点钱，也要坐飞机去。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ nìngyuàn duō huā diǎn qián, yě yào zuò fēijī qù.
examples.english: I would rather spend a bit more and go by plane.

examples.hanzi: 他宁愿饿着，也不吃不新鲜的东西。
examples.pinyin: Tā nìngyuàn è zhe, yě bù chī bù xīnxiān de dōngxi.
examples.english: He would rather go hungry than eat food that isn't fresh.

components.note: 阝 (mound, hill) — left-side 阝 is 阜 (mound), as in 阳, 院, 队; hiding behind a mound — 隐 is to conceal; the right side is a simplified stand-in.
目 (eye) — 目 is the eye, as in 看, 眼, 睛; 瞒 is hiding something from sight.
㒼 (mán) — same sound — 瞒 is mán; 㒼 also sounds out 满 mǎn.

example.hanzi: 他一直向父母隐瞒自己辞职的事。
example.pinyin: Tā yìzhí xiàng fùmǔ yǐnmán zìjǐ cízhí de shì.
example.english: He kept hiding the fact that he had quit his job from his parents.
example.fact: 隐瞒 almost always carries a negative charge — the thing hidden (a mistake, a diagnosis, the truth) is something that arguably should have been disclosed — unlike the neutral 保密 ("keep confidential"), which is often entirely proper, as with a trade secret.

examples.hanzi: 你为什么要隐瞒这件事？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ wèishénme yào yǐnmán zhè jiàn shì?
examples.english: Why do you want to hide this matter?

examples.hanzi: 他隐瞒了自己的真实年龄。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǐnmán le zìjǐ de zhēnshí niánlíng.
examples.english: He concealed his real age.

components.note: 见 (see) — seeing and vision: 看, 现, 视, 览; 观 is to watch. 又 only stands in for the old sound part 雚 (guàn).
灬 (fire) — heat and burning, as in 热 hot, 照 shine, 黑 black; a dot is a small spot like a spark.
占 (zhàn) is a loose sound clue for diǎn; 占 also sounds out 站 zhàn and 粘 zhān.

example.hanzi: 每个人对这个问题都有不同的观点。
example.pinyin: Měi gè rén duì zhège wèntí dōu yǒu bùtóng de guāndiǎn.
example.english: Everyone has a different point of view on this issue.
example.fact: 观 (built from 见 "to see" plus 又, a repeated hand motion) already means "to observe closely," and 点 traces back to a small dot or point of light — together 观点 builds "a point from which one observes," a fairly transparent path to the modern sense "viewpoint, standpoint."

examples.hanzi: 我不同意你的观点。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bù tóngyì nǐ de guāndiǎn.
examples.english: I don't agree with your point of view.

examples.hanzi: 从他的观点来看，这个计划不太现实。
examples.pinyin: Cóng tā de guāndiǎn lái kàn, zhège jìhuà bú tài xiànshí.
examples.english: From his point of view, this plan isn't very realistic.
